problem: 3D visual grounding datasets and models handle only object-centric, single-step descriptions, ignoring the multi-step, task-oriented, context-dependent nature of daily activities where later steps implicitly refer to earlier objects ("it", "here", "the other"). Existing multi-target navigation benchmarks (MultiON, GOAT-Bench) treat targets in a sequence as independent.
motivation: Embodied agents (SayCan/SayPlan style) decompose high-level tasks into sequential steps and must locate the right object at each step, using context to disambiguate same-category distractors. Current 3D-VG and navigation benchmarks do not test this. A manual study finds 20.7% of steps and 57.0% of tasks require context to disambiguate.
key_idea: Introduce the SG3D task and benchmark (task-oriented sequential grounding and navigation, with a navigation variant), and propose a 3D-LLM with a stepwise grounding paradigm and a sequential adapter that attends to previously predicted target objects.
insight: Sequential context matters a lot. Removing the task description and prior steps drops task accuracy by 7.7–13.9 points (40–60% relative) for grounding and by more than 40% relative for navigation. Reasoning LLMs (DeepSeek R1) beat plain LLMs and zero-shot 3D-VG models, but perception limits them. Fine-tuning raises step accuracy far more than task accuracy, and the memory-like sequential adapter helps mainly t-acc. In navigation, the end-to-end GRU policy retains context across steps and gains after fine-tuning, while the modular agent does not.
method: Dataset construction: SceneVerse-derived 3D scene graphs (category, attributes, spatial relations, captions) from ScanNet, ARKitScenes, 3RScan, MultiScan and HM3D are given to GPT-4, which generates 5 tasks per scene, each with a description and steps with one target object per step. Prompts use pronouns and in-context examples to induce contextual dependencies. Tasks over 10 steps are dropped.
Human verification: annotators check the evaluation set in a 3D mesh viewer. Tasks with one wrong step are revised, and tasks with multiple wrong steps are discarded.

Sequential navigation dataset: HM3D-based tasks are converted into Habitat-Sim episodes following GOAT-Bench. The Stretch robot has actions MOVE_FORWARD 0.25m, 30° turns and STOP, and each step succeeds if the agent stops within 1m of the target.

Stepwise grounding model: built on LEO with a Vicuna-7B backbone (LoRA rank 16). A spatial transformer tokenizes the scene into object tokens. For each step, the LLM generates the step instruction plus a [GRD]_i token, which is fed with the object tokens to a grounding head that predicts the target object.

Sequential adapter: per-layer learnable adapter tokens (K = max steps) are added to embeddings of previously predicted objects o_1..o_{i-1}, with future steps masked. An extra attention over these tokens is added to native self-attention via a zero-initialised tanh gate, in the style of LLaMA-Adapter.

Grounding baselines: 3D-VG models (MiKASA, ViewRefer, 3D-VisTA, PQ3D) take the task, prior steps and current step, with one pass per step, over PointNet++ features. LLMs (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-72B, DeepSeek V3/R1) get a JSON scene of predicted categories and boxes. Chat-Scene and GPT4Scene are also evaluated, on ScanNet only. All use GT object masks.

Navigation baselines: a modular Embodied VideoAgent that stores CLIP object memory and picks the highest cosine-similarity object given the task and steps. An end-to-end GOAT-Bench-style CLIP+GRU RL policy, trained for 70M steps.

setting.backbone: Vicuna-7B (LEO-style 3D LLM, LoRA fine-tuned) with a sequential adapter
setting.training_data: SG3D training split: 20,389 tasks / 103,100 steps over 5 scene datasets, 50 epochs. Navigation policy trained with RL on the navigation episodes for 70M steps.
setting.observation: Grounding: 3D scene object tokens from GT instance masks (point cloud). Navigation: egocentric RGB-D + pose + step text.
setting.action_space: Grounding: select an object instance ID per step. Navigation: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 30°, STOP.
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D scenes) for navigation; static scans for grounding
setting.privileged: Grounding uses ground-truth object instance masks (detection decoupled from grounding, following ReferIt3D); LLM baselines use predicted categories with GT boxes.

numbers_note: These are the paper's own benchmark, not one of the canonical benchmarks. The numbers listed are the paper's proposed model and its own navigation baselines. Per-dataset grounding numbers are in Table main-2. The context-removal ablation is only in a figure.
results: The proposed model gets 63.1 s-acc / 33.9 t-acc overall, beating the best fine-tuned baseline 3D-VisTA (60.9 / 29.5). Best zero-shot is GPT4Scene (56.0 / 18.7 on ScanNet only) and DeepSeek R1 (40.2 / 14.2 overall). Navigation is very weak (s-SR ≤ 14.7, t-SR ≤ 7.7) versus humans at 85% s-acc / 63% t-acc on grounding.
limitations: Grounding uses GT object masks and static scans. Chat-Scene and GPT4Scene are only evaluated on ScanNet, and the sequential model's planning ability is weak (GPT-4 score 2.1/5).
Tasks are GPT-4 generated, with human verification only on the evaluation set. Only one target object per step is allowed, and steps without an object reuse the previous target.
Navigation baselines are simple, with low absolute performance and no strong dedicated sequential navigation method.
